Nevis is one of our favorite islands, and we encourage you to explore Nevis beyond the small town to make the most of your visit! We offer several excellent and varied options for you to do so and still leave you with plenty of time on your own for the beach. Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

Philipsburg is the main town on the Dutch side of St. Maarten. The town is situated on a narrow stretch of land between Great Bay and the Great Salt Pond. Philipsburg was founded in 1763 by John Philips, a Scottish captain in the Dutch navy. The settlement soon became a center for international trade. The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. Depending on the traffic, SeaDream has the option to anchor or dock alongside. One of the highlight activities may be to participate in the America’s Cup 12 Metre Regatta.

voyages.title: Best of the Secluded Caribbean
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials From secluded beaches to dramatic volcanic landscapes and refined island harbors, this voyage reveals the Caribbean in all its contrasts. Sail from St. Thomas to Cruz Bay in St. John, where pristine beaches and protected national park lands set the tone, before arriving in Jost van Dyke for the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash®, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar on the soft sands of White Bay. Continue to Virgin Gorda from Spanish Town to Leverick Bay, allowing time to discover The Baths, where towering granite boulders create winding passages and sheltered pools along the shoreline. In Saba, a striking shift in scenery unfolds as steep green peaks rise directly from the sea, offering one of the Caribbean's most distinctive landscapes. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and waterfront cafés take on a more intimate feel after sunset. Call on Marigot, where French-Caribbean flair and seaside charm offer one final moment to savor, before your journey concludes back in St. Thomas, where Charlotte Amalie's vibrant harbor and historic streets offer a lively and colorful close to your time in the Caribbean.

The island has tons of history, beautiful beaches, a fantastic golf course and incredible shopping options.

It is blessed with many beautiful beaches and bays, fine anchorages and verdant hills. Enjoy the day with snorkeling trip to Trunk Bay with its underwater guided trail, or join our kayaking land adventure. Ask your Club Director for a guided hike to Caneel Bay stopping at beautiful Honeymoon Beach for a quiet swim. Rental Cars are available should you want to explore on your own or you could borrow a SeaDream Mountain Bike for independent exploration. From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

voyages.title: Best of the Leeward Islands
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Sail from San Juan through a series of relaxed harbors and sunlit shores, where each stop reveals a more unhurried side of the Caribbean. In Sandy Ground, calm waters and a quiet beach setting invite time to unwind, before continuing to Charlestown, where Nevis' lush, mountainous landscape and charming capital reflect a slower pace of island life. In St. Barths, enjoy an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and waterfront cafés take on a more intimate feel after sunset. Continue to Norman Island, where hidden coves and shimmering waters invite time to swim and explore, before arriving in Jost van Dyke for the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash®, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar on the soft sands of White Bay. Your journey concludes back in San Juan, where colorful streets and historic forts meet the vibrant energy of Puerto Rico.

SeaDream offers an opportunity to tee off, snorkel, or, for the energetic, bike around the island with the Club Director. Naturally, we will also offer water sports while we are anchored off Sandy Ground.

Nevis is one of our favorite islands, and we encourage you to explore Nevis beyond the small town to make the most of your visit! We offer several excellent and varied options for you to do so and still leave you with plenty of time on your own for the beach. Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

Norman Island is located at the southern tip of the British Virgin Islands. It could very well be the very same island reputed to be the inspiration for Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel Treasure Island. It is said that the island was named after a pirate who purchased it at some point during the early 18th century. The island is uninhabited and privately owned by Dr Henry Jarecki. Its area is about 600 acres (2.4 km²), and it is about 2.5 miles (4 km) long. A large harbor is known as "The Bight" offers one of the most protected anchorages in the area. Guests will enjoy some great hiking opportunities as well as snorkeling and scuba diving. Another attractive option may be to check out the Willie T that is generally anchored in the harbor or simply have a beverage at the Pirates Bight Bar.

voyages.title: Caribbean Celebration I
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Celebrate the season in the Caribbean, where warm breezes, sunlit shores, and unhurried days set the tone for a festive escape, an ideal setting for a Christmas spent by the sea. Depart San Juan for Cruz Bay in St. John, where some of the Caribbean's most pristine beaches unfold within a protected national park, inviting snorkeling, exploration, and unhurried afternoons. The French-Caribbean spirit of Marigot drifts through open-air markets and waterfront bistros, offering a taste of Riviera charm with a distinctly island soul. Gustavia, St. Barths, delivers an overnight of effortless elegance, its sheltered harbor framed by boutique-lined streets and candlelit cafés that glow warmly after sunset. In Virgin Gorda, two days from Spanish Town to Leverick Bay reveal the island at its most iconic, none more so than The Baths, where towering granite boulders give way to winding passages and sunlit sea pools. The voyage reaches a spirited high in Jost van Dyke, where the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® transforms White Bay's soft sands into an elegant seaside celebration of chilled champagne, indulgent caviar, and a leisurely beachside barbecue. Your journey concludes back in San Juan, where colorful streets and the holiday spirit carry the celebration ashore.

A territory of the Unites States, Puerto Rico is comprised of the large main island as well as five smaller islands, including the popular islands of Vieques and Culebra (both ports of call on select SeaDream voyages). SeaDream docks in Old San Juan, the oldest part of the city. Parts of this historic port city are still surrounded by stone walls dating back to the 1500’s. Narrow cobblestone streets, small shops, and points of interest like Cathedral of San Juan Bautista make this charming city a great place to stroll. Guests sailing into or departing from San Juan will enjoy views of Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, a mid- 1700’s Spanish fortress. San Juan Luiz Munoz Marin Airport is approximately a 30-minute drive to the port in Old San Juan. Currency in Puerto Rico is USD.

Two-thirds of St. John Island has been dedicated as a national park and is the most virgin of the U.S. Virgin Islands. It is blessed with many beautiful beaches and bays, fine anchorages and verdant hills. Enjoy the day with snorkeling trip to Trunk Bay with its underwater guided trail, or join our kayaking land adventure. Ask your Club Director for a guided hike to Caneel Bay stopping at beautiful Honeymoon Beach for a quiet swim. Rental Cars are available should you want to explore on your own or you could borrow a SeaDream Mountain Bike for independent exploration. From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

Marigot is the main town and capital on the French side of Saint Martin. The city of Marigot is perhaps the most French in spirit of all the cities in the Caribbean. Colonial houses stand beside cafés and bistros, pastry shops and luxury boutiques, and in many ways, it looks just like any of the French market towns you might expect to find in Europe. At the southern end of town by the harbor is Marina Port la Royale. This area includes elegant stores with the latest in European designer fashion and fine jewelry, all duty and tax-free. The entire city is only four streets wide, so it is very easy to get around. Marigot was named the capital during the reign of King Louis XVI, who built Fort St. Louis on a hill near Marigot Bay. Today, that building is the most important in the city. SeaDream anchors off Marigot and offers several yachting land adventures as well as the possibility to play with the toys at the marina.

Perhaps our most treasured destination in the Caribbean! This small island belonging to the French West Indies has so much to offer our SeaDream guests. Another great activity here is to simply relax and watch all of the incredible yachts arriving and departing just off your SeaDream yacht.

voyages.title: Tropical New Year's II
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Ring in the New Year in the Caribbean with extended time in St. Barths, where three days and two nights in Gustavia place you at the center of one of the region’s most vibrant holiday settings. Depart St. Thomas and arrive in St. Barths, where days unfold between sunlit beaches and harbor-side cafés, leading into festive evenings and a New Year’s celebration along a lively waterfront. Continue to St. Maarten, from Philipsburg to Simpson Bay and Sandy Ground, where a blend of Dutch and French-Caribbean influences creates a dynamic coastal experience, before sailing to Virgin Gorda from Spanish Town to Leverick Bay, with time to discover The Baths, where towering granite boulders form winding passages and sheltered pools along the shoreline. In Jost van Dyke, the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue. In St. John, Cruz Bay offers a final moment of calm with pristine beaches and protected waters, before returning to St. Thomas, where this celebratory voyage comes full circle.

Philipsburg is the main town on the Dutch side of St. Maarten. The town is situated on a narrow stretch of land between Great Bay and the Great Salt Pond. Philipsburg was founded in 1763 by John Philips, a Scottish captain in the Dutch navy. The settlement soon became a center for international trade. The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. Depending on the traffic, SeaDream has the option to anchor or dock alongside. One of the highlight activities may be to participate in the America’s Cup 12 Metre Regatta.

Simpson Bay straddles the best of both worlds, delivering white-sand beaches, beautiful lagoons dotted with impressive yachts, and vibrant dining spots that take in the energy of the island.

Anegada is the northernmost of the British Virgin Islands. It can be tricky to navigate too due to the shallow depths and various reefs upon arrival. While the other islands in the virgin islands group are mountainous, Anegada is flat. The highest point is only about 28 feet (8.5 m) above sea level, earning it the name which translates from Spanish as “the drowned land.” Anegada is the second largest of the British Virgin Islands, but it is also the most sparsely populated of the main islands (population roughly 200). The 18 mile long Horseshoe Reef happens to be the largest barrier coral reef in the Caribbean and believed to be the 4th largest on Earth.

Norman Island is located at the southern tip of the British Virgin Islands. It could very well be the very same island reputed to be the inspiration for Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel Treasure Island. It is said that the island was named after a pirate who purchased it at some point during the early 18th century. The island is uninhabited and privately owned by Dr Henry Jarecki. Its area is about 600 acres (2.4 km²), and it is about 2.5 miles (4 km) long. A large harbor is known as "The Bight" offers one of the most protected anchorages in the area. Guests will enjoy some great hiking opportunities as well as snorkeling and scuba diving. Another attractive option may be to check out the Willie T that is generally anchored in the harbor or simply have a beverage at the Pirates Bight Bar.

voyages.title: Spanish Caribbean & St. Barths Discovery
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Depart San Juan and spend the first day exploring Puerto Rico's quieter side, beginning in Culebra, where powdery white sand and impossibly clear water fringe a coastline that remains largely untouched, before continuing to Esperanza, a sun-bleached waterfront village on Vieques' southern coast where the malecón comes alive in the evening, just a short ride from Mosquito Bay, home to one of the world's brightest bioluminescent bays. In St. John, Cruz Bay opens to the lush protected landscapes of Virgin Islands National Park, where trails wind through tropical forest down to secluded beaches. In Philipsburg, the Dutch side of St. Maarten reveals a lively harbor town with colorful storefronts, duty-free shopping, and a long stretch of beach just steps from the waterfront. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where the harbor quiets after the day boats depart and boutique-lined streets, waterfront cafés, and candlelit restaurants take on a more intimate rhythm after sunset. In Jost van Dyke, the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun. Your journey returns full circle to San Juan, where the ease of a roundtrip voyage means you arrive exactly where you began, with nothing left to arrange.

San Juan Luiz Munoz Marin Airport is approximately a 30-minute drive to the port in Old San Juan. Currency in Puerto Rico is USD.

An 11-square-mile island off the northeast coast of Puerto Rico, Culebra is also home to the small adjacent uninhabited islands of Culebrita and Cayo Norte to the east and Luis Peña to the west. Culebra’s breathtaking beautiful Flamenco Beach regularly appears on lists of the “World’s Best Beaches.” Following your day exploring Culebra, that evening we invite you to Vieques Island, where you can kayak in bioluminescent waters filled with glittering sea organisms.

Esperanza is a charming “barrio” located on the south side of the island-municipality of Vieques, Puerto Rico. It is known for El Malecon, which means “The Strip,” the fishing tradition, the fight against the US Navy, and Esperanza Beach, one of the only locations in Isla de Vieques with restaurants and restrooms close by. Children enjoy jumping off the pier at the beach, and for those who enjoy good food and local entertainment without the hustle and bustle of a busy nightlife, El Malecon in Esperanza is the place to be. The island’s name, Vieques, is said to mean “small island” in Taino, and its nickname is Isla Nena, meaning “Little Girl Island”. Puerto Rico’s little sister island - Vieques measures 55 square feet with under 10,000 inhabitants. Along with Culebra and other various small islands, the archipelago makes up the Spanish Virgin Islands, or “Passage Islands.” Vieques was also referred to as “Crab Island” by the British. English and Spanish are both recognized as official languages of the area. As with the other Puerto Rican islands, pre-Columbian history is limited in clarity. Archaeologists believe Vieques was home to Native Americans who migrated from the American continent between 3000 and 2000 BCE. A fragmented human skeleton named “El Hombre de Puerto Ferro” was discovered northwest of the popular Bioluminescent Bay, estimated to be from 1900 BCE. Best known as the people in later centuries of Puerto Rico, the Taino culture was comprised of groups from Venezuela, Cuba, and Hispaniola, who migrated in waves up to 1000 AD. The Taino flourished until Europeans discovered Vieques in the 15th century - often credited to Christopher Columbus. Vieques became the center of the Taino rebellion against Spain, which ultimately ended in the Taino downfall. Despite this, Spain did not colonize for many centuries and Vieques, along with Culebra, became a sanctuary for pirates and outlaws. The French, Danish, Scottish, and English all attempted to secure Vieques but failed - Spain permanently settled by 1811. When the Spanish-American War concluded in 1898, Spain turned the Puerto Rican islands over to the United States, which by the 1940’s (post-WWII) served as a firing range for the Navy. Up until 2003, a multitude of protests continued for decades, pressuring the United Stated Navy enough to withdraw from the islands. Vieques is now a National Wildlife Refuge and growing tourist destination. Because of the lack of human interference, most of the areas previously closed off to civilians by the Navy feature over 40 gorgeous beaches, and many natural ecotourism locations for exploration. Blue Beach features an excellent place for snorkeling, Bioluminescent Bay has quickly become a popular spot for its notorious glowing dinoflagellates, and the island is also known for free-roaming 'feral paso fino 'horses.

The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. voyages.title: St. Barths Getaway
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials A roundtrip journey from St. Thomas that moves through the British Virgin Islands and beyond, anchoring at some of the northeastern Caribbean's most rewarding shores. North Sound opens with Virgin Gorda's expansive natural harbor, where calm protected waters and a striking landscape set a quietly immersive tone for the voyage ahead. Our Champagne & Caviar Splash® follows in Jost van Dyke, where chilled Champagne is served alongside caviar on the soft sands of White Bay, followed by a leisurely beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun. The voyage continues to St. Barths for a rare two-night stay in Gustavia, where the island's refined character and softly lit terraces reveal themselves fully once the harbor settles into its evening rhythm, with an additional day to explore at a leisurely pace. Cruz Bay provides a serene final stop in St. John, where the protected landscapes of Virgin Islands National Park offer a quiet close to the journey before returning to St. Thomas.

voyages.title: Best of British Virgin Isles & St. Barths
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Set out from San Juan on a roundtrip journey through some of the Caribbean's most rewarding anchorages. In St. John, Cruz Bay sits at the edge of Virgin Islands National Park, where coral-fringed shores and forested hillsides spill down to the water's edge. Saba rises next from the sea as a dramatic volcanic peak, its steep green slopes and near-carless roads offering a rare glimpse of the Caribbean entirely off the beaten path. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where the evening belongs to unhurried dinners, softly lit terraces, and the quiet elegance that defines the island after the day trippers have gone. Spend a in Virgin Gorda, from Spanish Town to Leverick Bay, where the island rewards those who linger, whether tracing the shoreline by water or exploring the interior at a leisurely pace. In Jost van Dyke, the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun. Experience a final night at anchor in Norman Island, where hidden coves and calm waters invite one last swim, before returning to San Juan.

This Caribbean paradise is a special municipality of the Netherlands. With an estimated local population of just over 2,000 people, Saba is now primarily supported by tourism, and is known for a concentration on “eco-tourism”. This includes diving, hiking, and climbing its mountainous terrain. The island is so small that there is only 1 main road, and its airport is well-known for having one of the shortest commercial runways in the world. The island’s intimate size, picturesque Red rooftops and lush vegetation make it a perfect port to call on during your special Caribbean yachting vacation.

voyages.title: Leeward Islands & Grenadines Discovery
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials From St. Thomas, this southward journey traces the full length of the eastern Caribbean, moving through the Virgin Islands and beyond as the islands grow quieter and more secluded with each passing day. Cruz Bay opens with the lush protected shores of Virgin Islands National Park before continuing to Spanish Town, where Virgin Gorda's unhurried character sets a relaxed tone, and Norman Island, where calm sheltered waters and hidden coves invite time to swim and explore. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces take on a more intimate rhythm once the harbor settles into evening. South Friars Bay reveals a quieter, more secluded stretch of golden sand framed by St. Kitts' volcanic hills, before continuing to Terre-de-Haut, where bougainvillea-draped lanes and a harbor ringed by green hills create a scene more reminiscent of provincial France than the tropics. An overnight in Bequia reveals Port Elizabeth's crescent harbor, handcrafted wooden boats, and the gentle rhythm of island life that makes it the Grenadines' most beloved anchorage. The Tobago Cays follow with crystalline waters and thriving coral gardens protected within a horseshoe reef, before Mayreau's tiny population and untouched shoreline offer one final moment of stillness before arrival in Bridgetown, where Barbados welcomes with its distinctive blend of British heritage and Caribbean warmth.

voyages.title: Leeward Islands & St. Barths Escape
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Puerto Rico's outer islands set the tone for this roundtrip journey from San Juan, beginning in Culebra, where crystalline waters and an unhurried pace reveal a quieter side of the Caribbean, before continuing to Esperanza, a sun-bleached waterfront village on Vieques' southern coast where the malecón comes alive in the evening and the surrounding bay shimmers with bioluminescence after dark. In St. John, Cruz Bay opens to the protected forests and reef-lined shores of Virgin Islands National Park, where the land meets the sea in near-pristine condition. Marigot follows with the relaxed sophistication of the French side of St. Martin, where open-air markets, waterfront bistros, and a laid-back harbor invite an afternoon of wandering. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces take on a more intimate character once the harbor settles into evening. In Jost van Dyke, the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun before returning to San Juan.

days.note: San Juan, founded in the 1520’s by Spanish settlers, is both the largest city and the capital city of Puerto Rico. A territory of the Unites States, Puerto Rico is comprised of the large main island as well as five smaller islands, including the popular islands of Vieques and Culebra (both ports of call on select SeaDream voyages). SeaDream docks in Old San Juan, the oldest part of the city. Parts of this historic port city are still surrounded by stone walls dating back to the 1500’s. Narrow cobblestone streets, small shops, and points of interest like Cathedral of San Juan Bautista make this charming city a great place to stroll. Guests sailing into or departing from San Juan will enjoy views of Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, a mid- 1700’s Spanish fortress. San Juan Luiz Munoz Marin Airport is approximately a 30-minute drive to the port in Old San Juan. Currency in Puerto Rico is USD.

An 11-square-mile island off the northeast coast of Puerto Rico, Culebra is also home to the small adjacent uninhabited islands of Culebrita and Cayo Norte to the east and Luis Peña to the west. Culebra’s breathtaking beautiful Flamenco Beach regularly appears on lists of the “World’s Best Beaches.” Following your day exploring Culebra, that evening we invite you to Vieques Island, where you can kayak in bioluminescent waters filled with glittering sea organisms.

Esperanza is a charming “barrio” located on the south side of the island-municipality of Vieques, Puerto Rico. It is known for El Malecon, which means “The Strip,” the fishing tradition, the fight against the US Navy, and Esperanza Beach, one of the only locations in Isla de Vieques with restaurants and restrooms close by. Children enjoy jumping off the pier at the beach, and for those who enjoy good food and local entertainment without the hustle and bustle of a busy nightlife, El Malecon in Esperanza is the place to be. The island’s name, Vieques, is said to mean “small island” in Taino, and its nickname is Isla Nena, meaning “Little Girl Island”. Puerto Rico’s little sister island - Vieques measures 55 square feet with under 10,000 inhabitants. Along with Culebra and other various small islands, the archipelago makes up the Spanish Virgin Islands, or “Passage Islands.” Vieques was also referred to as “Crab Island” by the British. English and Spanish are both recognized as official languages of the area. As with the other Puerto Rican islands, pre-Columbian history is limited in clarity. Archaeologists believe Vieques was home to Native Americans who migrated from the American continent between 3000 and 2000 BCE. A fragmented human skeleton named “El Hombre de Puerto Ferro” was discovered northwest of the popular Bioluminescent Bay, estimated to be from 1900 BCE. Best known as the people in later centuries of Puerto Rico, the Taino culture was comprised of groups from Venezuela, Cuba, and Hispaniola, who migrated in waves up to 1000 AD. The Taino flourished until Europeans discovered Vieques in the 15th century - often credited to Christopher Columbus. Vieques became the center of the Taino rebellion against Spain, which ultimately ended in the Taino downfall. Despite this, Spain did not colonize for many centuries and Vieques, along with Culebra, became a sanctuary for pirates and outlaws. The French, Danish, Scottish, and English all attempted to secure Vieques but failed - Spain permanently settled by 1811. When the Spanish-American War concluded in 1898, Spain turned the Puerto Rican islands over to the United States, which by the 1940’s (post-WWII) served as a firing range for the Navy. Up until 2003, a multitude of protests continued for decades, pressuring the United Stated Navy enough to withdraw from the islands. Vieques is now a National Wildlife Refuge and growing tourist destination. Because of the lack of human interference, most of the areas previously closed off to civilians by the Navy feature over 40 gorgeous beaches, and many natural ecotourism locations for exploration. Blue Beach features an excellent place for snorkeling, Bioluminescent Bay has quickly become a popular spot for its notorious glowing dinoflagellates, and the island is also known for free-roaming 'feral paso fino 'horses.

Two-thirds of St. John Island has been dedicated as a national park and is the most virgin of the U.S. Virgin Islands. It is blessed with many beautiful beaches and bays, fine anchorages and verdant hills. Enjoy the day with snorkeling trip to Trunk Bay with its underwater guided trail, or join our kayaking land adventure. Ask your Club Director for a guided hike to Caneel Bay stopping at beautiful Honeymoon Beach for a quiet swim. Rental Cars are available should you want to explore on your own or you could borrow a SeaDream Mountain Bike for independent exploration. From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

Colonial houses stand beside cafés and bistros, pastry shops and luxury boutiques, and in many ways, it looks just like any of the French market towns you might expect to find in Europe. At the southern end of town by the harbor is Marina Port la Royale. This area includes elegant stores with the latest in European designer fashion and fine jewelry, all duty and tax-free. The entire city is only four streets wide, so it is very easy to get around. Marigot was named the capital during the reign of King Louis XVI, who built Fort St. Louis on a hill near Marigot Bay. In Îles des Saintes, bougainvillea-draped lanes and a harbor ringed by green hills create a scene more reminiscent of provincial France than the tropics, before Charlestown reveals Nevis at its most unhurried and South Friars Bay offers a quieter stretch of golden sand framed by St. Kitts' volcanic hills. Our signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay in Jost van Dyke, where chilled champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun before the journey concludes in St. Thomas.

Once one of the island's most vital trading ports, it earned the nickname "Little Bristol" for its deep ties to English commerce. Wander the streets past coral-stone buildings and wooden-balconied facades, or step inside the Arlington House Museum for a vivid account of the island's history. St. Pierre, Martinique, nestled at the foot of Mount Pelée on the island’s lush northwest coast, is a captivating blend of natural beauty and rich history—perfect for culture lovers, history buffs, and those seeking an off-the-beaten-path escape. Once dubbed the “Paris of the Caribbean,” and “City of Art and History,” this seaside town offers a unique mix of French-Creole charm and dramatic volcanic legacy. Explore the open-air ruins left by the 1902 eruption, visit science museums and the prestigious Depaz & Neisson rum distillery, and stroll cobblestone streets lined with colonial remnants and vibrant local markets. Just offshore, divers can explore historic shipwrecks resting beneath turquoise waters, while nearby black-sand beaches and rainforest trails offer moments of quiet seclusion. Your yacht drops anchor just steps away from town, with easy access to Martinique’s many charms.

Nevis is one of our favorite islands, and we encourage you to explore Nevis beyond the small town to make the most of your visit! We offer several excellent and varied options for you to do so and still leave you with plenty of time on your own for the beach. Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

Cruz Bay opens the voyage with St. John's coral-fringed beaches and forested trails, a quiet introduction to the days ahead. Saba follows as one of the Caribbean's most singular islands, its steep green slopes and near-carless roads rising sharply from the sea and offering a rare glimpse of life entirely off the beaten path. The pace slows further in Gustavia, where an overnight stay in St. Barths reveals boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces best appreciated once the day trippers have gone. Two days in Virgin Gorda follow, from Spanish Town to Leverick Bay, with time to discover the island's sheltered bays and dramatic granite landscapes at a leisurely pace. The signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds next in Jost van Dyke, where chilled champagne and caviar are served on the soft sands of White Bay, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the water. The voyage draws to a close with one final night at anchor in Norman Island, its hidden coves offering one last swim before returning to San Juan.

days.note: San Juan, founded in the 1520’s by Spanish settlers, is both the largest city and the capital city of Puerto Rico. A territory of the Unites States, Puerto Rico is comprised of the large main island as well as five smaller islands, including the popular islands of Vieques and Culebra (both ports of call on select SeaDream voyages). SeaDream docks in Old San Juan, the oldest part of the city. Parts of this historic port city are still surrounded by stone walls dating back to the 1500’s. Narrow cobblestone streets, small shops, and points of interest like Cathedral of San Juan Bautista make this charming city a great place to stroll. Guests sailing into or departing from San Juan will enjoy views of Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, a mid- 1700’s Spanish fortress. San Juan Luiz Munoz Marin Airport is approximately a 30-minute drive to the port in Old San Juan. Currency in Puerto Rico is USD.

Two-thirds of St. John Island has been dedicated as a national park and is the most virgin of the U.S. Virgin Islands. It is blessed with many beautiful beaches and bays, fine anchorages and verdant hills. Enjoy the day with snorkeling trip to Trunk Bay with its underwater guided trail, or join our kayaking land adventure. Ask your Club Director for a guided hike to Caneel Bay stopping at beautiful Honeymoon Beach for a quiet swim. Rental Cars are available should you want to explore on your own or you could borrow a SeaDream Mountain Bike for independent exploration. From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

This Caribbean paradise is a special municipality of the Netherlands. Due to this fact, Saba is actually the location of the tallest, or highest point/elevation of the Netherlands, even though it is a few thousand miles away from its European homeland. With an estimated local population of just over 2,000 people, Saba is now primarily supported by tourism, and is known for a concentration on “eco-tourism”. This includes diving, hiking, and climbing its mountainous terrain. The island is so small that there is only 1 main road, and its airport is well-known for having one of the shortest commercial runways in the world. The island’s intimate size, picturesque Red rooftops and lush vegetation make it a perfect port to call on during your special Caribbean yachting vacation.

voyages.title: Eastern Caribbean Discovery
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials San Juan gives way to open water as this southward passage through the Caribbean begins, each island revealing a different shade of the region's character. In St. John, Cruz Bay opens to the quiet beauty of Virgin Islands National Park, where forested hillsides meet reef-lined shores in near-pristine condition. Virgin Gorda follows in Spanish Town, where the island's unhurried character sets the tone before arriving at Norman Island, where calm, sheltered waters and hidden coves invite time to swim and explore. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where the harbor takes on a softer rhythm after sunset, and boutique-lined streets and candlelit terraces reward those who linger into the evening. South Friars Bay reveals a quieter, more secluded stretch of golden sand framed by St. Kitts' volcanic hills, before continuing to Terre-de-Haut, the smallest and most visited of the Îles des Saintes, where bougainvillea-draped streets, a picturesque harbor, and a distinctly French character make for one of the eastern Caribbean's most charming stops. Spend two days in Bequia, where Port Elizabeth's crescent bay, wooden fishing boats, and unhurried village life embody the Grenadines at their most authentic. The Tobago Cays follow with some of the Caribbean's most celebrated snorkeling waters, protected within a horseshoe of coral reef, before Mayreau offers one final quiet anchorage, its tiny population and untouched shoreline a fitting prelude to arrival in Bridgetown, where Barbados welcomes with its distinctive blend of British heritage and Caribbean warmth.

South Friar's Bay offers SeaDream guests a new way to explore the island of St. Kitts. Rather than docking at the capital, the yacht will be anchored in the bay. This particular bay is one of the two bays stretching along the coast of the isthmus connecting the Southeast Peninsula, with the rest of the island of Saint Kitts. From swimming and snorkeling on the south side to body surfing on the north, Friar's Bay offers guests several options. Many locals consider the southern beach the best on the island. If you are thirsty, no worries as there are multiple beach bars, offering various food and beverage options. The island itself offers several land adventure options including the Unesco Awarded Brimstone Fortress, Zip Lines, off road adventures and golf at the Royal St. Kitts.

days.port: Terre De Haut, Îles des Saintes
days.note: If you’re looking for a small part of France in the heart of Guadeloupe, Terre de Haut is your go-to. Being the largest of the eight small islands that make up Les Saintes, Terre de Haut is a charming and scenic village rich with red-roofed houses and accompanying gardens of flourishing Hibiscus. Known for its robust reefs and great underwater visibility, Terre de Haut has also become a favorite among divers.

Bequia is the northernmost and largest of the Grenadines, just seven square miles of quiet lagoons, reefs, and long silvery stretches of beach. Among the first things you will notice are the colorful model boats set up on stands around the tiny harbor, representing the island's maritime history. If you are lucky enough to have a late call, don’t miss Mac’s Lobster Pizza.

Imagine an intimate cluster of five uninhabited islands, heavenly lagoons full of green turtles, coral reefs, colorful fish and crystal clear waters. This is the setting when SeaDream anchors off the Tobago Cays. Zodiacs will whisk guests from the marina to the beautiful beach. There may be some locals selling crafts so remember to bring some dollars. This is an idyllic yachting anchorage, a dream for scuba divers, a paradise for beachcombers, and a film location for the Pirates of the Caribbean, the Tobago Cays and the Tobago Cays Marine Park is one of the world’s most awe inspiring island destinations.

Accessible only by yacht and small sailboats, Mayreau is the smallest public island of the Grenadines, with an area of about .46 square miles and a population of less than 300, centered in an unnamed village on a hilltop in the southwest of the island—its highest point and a nice hike from Saline Beach, where SeaDream anchors. Surrounded by magnificent coral reefs and gorgeous beaches, Mayreau and its surrounding Tobago Cays waters sit in a nationally protected area that has experienced a resurgence of marine life, including turtles that swim and feed while you mingle with and observe them. Take in the flora and fauna and don’t miss some of the best snorkeling in the world. Perhaps the ideal spot to anchor, Saline Bay provides easy access to Saline Bay Beach and Salt Whistle Bay Beach, a rare double-sided beach.

SeaDream uses the port of Bridgetown as the hub for their Southern Caribbean voyages as well as some voyages that cross the Atlantic. The Island itself includes UNESCO Heritage Sites, excellent beaches and history dating back to 1628. The climate is tropical with constant warm temperatures during the year cooled by light trade winds.

voyages.title: Best of the British Leewards & St. Barths
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials This roundtrip journey from St. Thomas brings together some of the Caribbean's most coveted experiences, anchoring at rewarding shores across the BVI, Anguilla, and St. Barths. Norman Island opens the voyage with calm sheltered waters and hidden coves that invite time to swim and explore, before Anegada reveals the BVI's most remote and distinctive island, its flat coral landscape, pink flamingos, and legendary reef a world apart from the volcanic peaks that define the rest of the archipelago. Sandy Ground introduces Anguilla at its most relaxed, where calm turquoise water and a laid-back shoreline invite time to unwind before continuing to St. Barths for a rare two-night stay in Gustavia, where the island's refined character and softly lit terraces reveal themselves fully once the harbor settles into its evening rhythm, with two full days to explore boutique-lined streets and waterfront cafés at a leisurely pace. White Bay in Jost van Dyke provides a sun-drenched finale, where our Champagne & Caviar Splash® sees chilled Champagne and caviar served on the sand, followed by a leisurely beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the water before returning to St. Thomas.

Anegada is the northernmost of the British Virgin Islands. It can be tricky to navigate too due to the shallow depths and various reefs upon arrival. While the other islands in the virgin islands group are mountainous, Anegada is flat. The highest point is only about 28 feet (8.5 m) above sea level, earning it the name which translates from Spanish as “the drowned land.” Anegada is the second largest of the British Virgin Islands, but it is also the most sparsely populated of the main islands (population roughly 200). The 18 mile long Horseshoe Reef happens to be the largest barrier coral reef in the Caribbean and believed to be the 4th largest on Earth.

This British Overseas Territory is becoming more popular due to the incredible resort options as well as world recognized beaches and amazing golf. SeaDream offers an opportunity to tee off, snorkel, or, for the energetic, bike around the island with the Club Director. Philipsburg is the main town on the Dutch side of St. Maarten. The town is situated on a narrow stretch of land between Great Bay and the Great Salt Pond. Philipsburg was founded in 1763 by John Philips, a Scottish captain in the Dutch navy. The settlement soon became a center for international trade. The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. Depending on the traffic, SeaDream has the option to anchor or dock alongside. One of the highlight activities may be to participate in the America’s Cup 12 Metre Regatta.

Perhaps our most treasured destination in the Caribbean! This small island belonging to the French West Indies has so much to offer our SeaDream guests. Incredible shopping only steps away from the pier. Incredible beaches, resorts, restaurants and activities both day and night. SeaDream has created various land adventures for you to discover the island from sea or land. Ask one of the officers to take you on a hike or bike ride around the island. Another great activity here is to simply relax and watch all of the incredible yachts arriving and departing just off your SeaDream yacht.

Nevis is one of our favorite islands, and we encourage you to explore Nevis beyond the small town to make the most of your visit! We offer several excellent and varied options for you to do so and still leave you with plenty of time on your own for the beach. Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

voyages.title: The Glorious Grenadines
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials This roundtrip journey from Bridgetown offers an immersive passage through the Grenadines, beginning with a quieter look at Barbados itself before the yacht traces a path through some of the southern Caribbean's most unspoiled waters. Speightstown offers a gentler introduction to the island's northern reaches, where chattel houses, a historic fishing pier, and a relaxed pace of life feel a world away from the capital. In Soufriere Bay, St. Lucia's volcanic drama comes into full view, the twin Pitons rising sharply from the water's edge while the surrounding hillsides tumble down in deep tropical green. Kingstown follows with St. Vincent's compact, colorful capital, where the Saturday market spills through the streets and the botanical gardens, among the oldest in the western hemisphere, reward a morning's exploration. Mount Wynne Beach offers a more secluded St. Vincent experience, a quiet black-sand shore framed by forested hills and accessible only by sea. Spend two days in Bequia, where Port Elizabeth's crescent harbor, handcrafted wooden boats, and the gentle rhythm of island life make it the Grenadines' most beloved anchorage. The Tobago Cays unfold next across a protected marine park, where crystalline water and thriving coral gardens make for some of the Caribbean's finest snorkeling, before Mayreau, one of the smallest inhabited islands in the Grenadines, provides a last moment of stillness before the return to Bridgetown.

days.note: SeaDream uses the port of Bridgetown as the hub for their Southern Caribbean voyages as well as some voyages that cross the Atlantic. The Island itself includes UNESCO Heritage Sites, excellent beaches and history dating back to 1628. The climate is tropical with constant warm temperatures during the year cooled by light trade winds.

Tucked along the calm northwest shore of Barbados, Speightstown carries the easy confidence of a town that has seen centuries pass without losing its identity. Arriving by yacht, you come ashore the way the port was always meant to be approached: without the crowds, without the queues, and with the whole of this unhurried town to yourselves. Once one of the island's most vital trading ports, it earned the nickname "Little Bristol" for its deep ties to English commerce. Wander the streets past coral-stone buildings and wooden-balconied facades, or step inside the Arlington House Museum for a vivid account of the island's history. When the afternoon calls for something slower, the clear Caribbean waters and quiet beaches at the edge of town answer readily.

Soufriere, a small town on the South West Coast of Saint Lucia is considered by many as the island’s gem. The town and the surrounding region has a population of 8,000. Originally founded by the French, it was the original capital of the island. Soufriere has a great deal to offer visitors including coral reefs, the rainforest, Diamond Falls, the sulfur springs, a “drive-in” volcano and the ever popular and majestic twin pitons. Check the Land Adventure options as we feel certain you will enjoy them. You may also sit back in one of the Balinese dream beds and witness a beautiful sunset.

A sheltered Island with a wild black-sand beach located on the Caribbean coast of St. Vincent, Mt. Wynne provides some of the best snorkeling opportunities in the southern Caribbean. The St. Vincent waters are a haven for flourishing reefs rich in marine life, boasting dozens of miles of coral reefs that are home to 400 fish species.

Bequia is the northernmost and largest of the Grenadines, just seven square miles of quiet lagoons, reefs, and long silvery stretches of beach. Among the first things you will notice are the colorful model boats set up on stands around the tiny harbor, representing the island's maritime history. If you are lucky enough to have a late call, don’t miss Mac’s Lobster Pizza.

Imagine an intimate cluster of five uninhabited islands, heavenly lagoons full of green turtles, coral reefs, colorful fish and crystal clear waters. This is the setting when SeaDream anchors off the Tobago Cays. Zodiacs will whisk guests from the marina to the beautiful beach. There may be some locals selling crafts so remember to bring some dollars. This is an idyllic yachting anchorage, a dream for scuba divers, a paradise for beachcombers, and a film location for the Pirates of the Caribbean, the Tobago Cays and the Tobago Cays Marine Park is one of the world’s most awe inspiring island destinations.

Accessible only by yacht and small sailboats, Mayreau is the smallest public island of the Grenadines, with an area of about .46 square miles and a population of less than 300, centered in an unnamed village on a hilltop in the southwest of the island—its highest point and a nice hike from Saline Beach, where SeaDream anchors. Surrounded by magnificent coral reefs and gorgeous beaches, Mayreau and its surrounding Tobago Cays waters sit in a nationally protected area that has experienced a resurgence of marine life, including turtles that swim and feed while you mingle with and observe them. Take in the flora and fauna and don’t miss some of the best snorkeling in the world. Perhaps the ideal spot to anchor, Saline Bay provides easy access to Saline Bay Beach and Salt Whistle Bay Beach, a rare double-sided beach.

voyages.title: British Leewards & St. Barths Discovery
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Sail from St. Thomas through a series of sun-drenched anchorages and refined island stops, where each port reveals a different expression of the northeastern Caribbean. In Sandy Ground, Anguilla's calm turquoise waters and laid-back shoreline invite time to unwind before continuing to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces take on a more intimate rhythm once the harbor settles into evening. Two days in Virgin Gorda follow, from Spanish Town to North Sound, where the island's sheltered bays and striking landscapes reward those who linger. In Norman Island, calm sheltered waters and hidden coves invite time to swim and explore at a leisurely pace. Your journey concludes in Jost van Dyke, where our signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, with chilled champagne and caviar served on the sand, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the water before returning to St. Thomas.

St. Pierre, Martinique, nestled at the foot of Mount Pelée on the island’s lush northwest coast, is a captivating blend of natural beauty and rich history—perfect for culture lovers, history buffs, and those seeking an off-the-beaten-path escape. Once dubbed the “Paris of the Caribbean,” and “City of Art and History,” this seaside town offers a unique mix of French-Creole charm and dramatic volcanic legacy. Explore the open-air ruins left by the 1902 eruption, visit science museums and the prestigious Depaz & Neisson rum distillery, and stroll cobblestone streets lined with colonial remnants and vibrant local markets. Just offshore, divers can explore historic shipwrecks resting beneath turquoise waters, while nearby black-sand beaches and rainforest trails offer moments of quiet seclusion. Your yacht drops anchor just steps away from town, with easy access to Martinique’s many charms.

Known for its robust reefs and great underwater visibility, Terre de Haut has also become a favorite among divers.

South Friar's Bay offers SeaDream guests a new way to explore the island of St. Kitts. Rather than docking at the capital, the yacht will be anchored in the bay. This particular bay is one of the two bays stretching along the coast of the isthmus connecting the Southeast Peninsula, with the rest of the island of Saint Kitts. From swimming and snorkeling on the south side to body surfing on the north, Friar's Bay offers guests several options. Many locals consider the southern beach the best on the island. If you are thirsty, no worries as there are multiple beach bars, offering various food and beverage options. voyages.title: St. Barths & Leeward Islands Delight
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials The Leeward Islands set an unhurried pace on this roundtrip journey from St. Thomas, where each stop reveals a slower, more reflective side of the Caribbean. In St. John, Cruz Bay opens to the protected forests and reef-lined shores of Virgin Islands National Park, where the land remains largely untouched. The Dutch waterfront of Philipsburg follows with colorful storefronts and a bustling harbor, a lively contrast before the calm of St. Barths takes over for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces settle into their evening rhythm once the harbor quiets. In Charlestown, Nevis reveals its volcanic interior and black-sand shoreline, a quieter island that rewards those who venture beyond the pier and into its Georgian streets. Norman Island offers one final calm anchorage, its hidden coves and sheltered waters inviting a last swim before the signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® closes the voyage on the soft sands of White Bay in Jost van Dyke, where chilled champagne and caviar give way to an elegant beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the sun before returning to St. Thomas.

Philipsburg is the main town on the Dutch side of St. Maarten. The town is situated on a narrow stretch of land between Great Bay and the Great Salt Pond. Philipsburg was founded in 1763 by John Philips, a Scottish captain in the Dutch navy. The settlement soon became a center for international trade. The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. Depending on the traffic, SeaDream has the option to anchor or dock alongside. One of the highlight activities may be to participate in the America’s Cup 12 Metre Regatta.

Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

voyages.title: Spanish Caribbean & the Virgin Isles
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Puerto Rico's southern coast comes into focus early on this roundtrip from San Juan, with Salinas revealing a more secluded side of the island before the journey continues into the British Virgin Islands. In Jost van Dyke, our Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled Champagne is served alongside caviar, followed by a leisurely beachside barbecue and time to linger in the water and sun. Norman Island follows with calm, sheltered waters and hidden coves that invite time to swim and explore, before the journey continues to North Sound, where Virgin Gorda's expansive natural harbor opens to some of the most protected and peaceful anchorage in the Caribbean. The voyage concludes with an overnight stay in Gustavia, where St. Barths' boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces reward an unhurried evening before returning to San Juan.

days.note: San Juan, founded in the 1520’s by Spanish settlers, is both the largest city and the capital city of Puerto Rico. A territory of the Unites States, Puerto Rico is comprised of the large main island as well as five smaller islands, including the popular islands of Vieques and Culebra (both ports of call on select SeaDream voyages). SeaDream docks in Old San Juan, the oldest part of the city. Parts of this historic port city are still surrounded by stone walls dating back to the 1500’s. Narrow cobblestone streets, small shops, and points of interest like Cathedral of San Juan Bautista make this charming city a great place to stroll. Guests sailing into or departing from San Juan will enjoy views of Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, a mid- 1700’s Spanish fortress. San Juan Luiz Munoz Marin Airport is approximately a 30-minute drive to the port in Old San Juan. Currency in Puerto Rico is USD.

Located on the southern coast of Puerto Rico, Salinas is defined by its rich fishing culture, breathtaking bay, and beautiful beaches. Piedras del Callado, a geological formation known to locals as Las Tetas de Cayey, is a designated nature reserve, perfect for hiking. Because Puerto Rico is an archipelago, it is surrounded by dozens of islets and cays, including Cayo Matías, a small mangrove island accessible by boat. Salinas is also home to the Olympic training center Albergue Olímpico, the Puerto Rican Museum of Sports, and a botanical garden. Known as the land of mojo isleño, its signature savory sauce used to marinate fish, Salinas is a gastronomic gem that’s bursting with bistros offering up fresh seafood dishes and traditional Puerto Rican fare. The Central Aguirre Historic District has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 2002. Today, over 400 cultural landmarks survive in various states of repair in Central Aguirre, including a sugar mill, plazas, wooden houses, and churches.

The BVI’s barefoot island and home of the "Painkiller" drink. Population depends on the month – typically 250-300. This is another SeaDream destination where you may be served Champagne & Caviar Splash® followed by a beach barbecue lunch. A hike is always offered to guests to visit the famous Foxy’s Bar at Great Harbour (hopefully, the boutique is open) or you can stroll a few meters down the beach to the Soggy Dollar Bar. Snorkeling equipment is provided as well as some of our water toys!

Norman Island is located at the southern tip of the British Virgin Islands. It could very well be the very same island reputed to be the inspiration for Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel Treasure Island. It is said that the island was named after a pirate who purchased it at some point during the early 18th century. The island is uninhabited and privately owned by Dr Henry Jarecki. Its area is about 600 acres (2.4 km²), and it is about 2.5 miles (4 km) long. A large harbor is known as "The Bight" offers one of the most protected anchorages in the area. Guests will enjoy some great hiking opportunities as well as snorkeling and scuba diving. Another attractive option may be to check out the Willie T that is generally anchored in the harbor or simply have a beverage at the Pirates Bight Bar.

Nearly every publication written about Virgin Gorda lists “The Baths” –as a must see! SeaDream generally arrives early and anchor’s off Spanish Town to give guests an early start to view the Baths before all of the tourists arrive from the neighboring Islands. You may also consider excellent Scuba Diving options or an opportunity to swim with dolphins. After our short “technical stop” to dispatch land adventures and clearance with the officials, SeaDream navigates scenically up the coast and arrives at North Sound to anchor just off the Bitter End Yacht Club. Here we offer water sports, land adventures, hiking options with the officers and tenders to the Bitter End!

voyages.title: St. Barths & Leeward Islands Delight
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials A roundtrip journey from St. Thomas that moves through the Leeward Islands and beyond, each anchorage offering a distinct character and a different pace. Cruz Bay opens with the lush, protected landscapes of Virgin Islands National Park, where forested trails wind down to coral-fringed shores. Philipsburg follows with the lively energy of St. Maarten's Dutch waterfront, where colorful storefronts and a bustling harbor provide a vibrant contrast before continuing to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces settle into a more intimate rhythm once the harbor quiets for the evening. Charlestown reveals Nevis at its most unhurried, where Georgian architecture, a black-sand shoreline, and a lush volcanic interior reward those who venture beyond the pier. Norman Island follows with calm sheltered waters and hidden coves that invite time to swim and explore, before our signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® brings the voyage to a memorable close on the soft sands of White Bay in Jost van Dyke, where chilled champagne and caviar are served alongside an elegant beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the water before returning to St. Thomas.

It is blessed with many beautiful beaches and bays, fine anchorages and verdant hills. Enjoy the day with snorkeling trip to Trunk Bay with its underwater guided trail, or join our kayaking land adventure. Ask your Club Director for a guided hike to Caneel Bay stopping at beautiful Honeymoon Beach for a quiet swim. Rental Cars are available should you want to explore on your own or you could borrow a SeaDream Mountain Bike for independent exploration. From Cruz Bay, we offer several Yachting Land Adventures specially created for SeaDream guests, including an exclusive experience at the Lovango Resort & Beach Club, tucked away on a private island just off St. John.

Philipsburg is the main town on the Dutch side of St. Maarten. The town is situated on a narrow stretch of land between Great Bay and the Great Salt Pond. Philipsburg was founded in 1763 by John Philips, a Scottish captain in the Dutch navy. The settlement soon became a center for international trade. The main shopping district is located on Front Street and is in the heart of the city. Many consider Philipsburg to be the best shopping opportunity in the Caribbean. Depending on the traffic, SeaDream has the option to anchor or dock alongside. One of the highlight activities may be to participate in the America’s Cup 12 Metre Regatta.

Nevis is one of our favorite islands, and we encourage you to explore Nevis beyond the small town to make the most of your visit! We offer several excellent and varied options for you to do so and still leave you with plenty of time on your own for the beach. Less commercial and laidback than its large neighbor St. Kitts, Nevis, at first glimpse, offers a stunning approach with dramatic views of the potentially active volcanic Nevis Peak (3,232 feet/985 meters). Your SeaDream tender will bring you within a few steps of the small town center. Charlestown does not offer too many sightseeing or shopping opportunities though the house where American statesman Alexander Hamilton was born is only a short walk away along the waterfront (now the Museum of Nevis History). To enjoy Nevis to its full potential, we recommend that you divide your day into Morning, Lunch/Afternoon and Evening activities. Morning - Start your day by exploring the island, above or under water, on one of our fun optional Land Adventures. They are all enjoyable & exciting, and you will also support the local community. The Four Seasons Resort still offers incredible golf options as well as beautiful beach and dining facilities. Another option for lunch is the L'Escale French Caribbean-style bistro, just down the road near the Oualie Pier. Evening - For a romantic sunset with cocktails and a snack or dinner, we like to take the short drive to see Gillian, the owner of the charming Bananas Restaurant, which offers lovely views surrounded by lush tropical gardens. Of course, there is also Sunshine's Beach Bar & Grill, home of the famous "Killer Bee" Caribbean rum drink. We hope that the above recommendations allow you to plan your special day on Nevis. Now, all you have to do is to decide which of the optional morning activities to join.

voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials A rare two-night stay in St. Barths anchors this journey from St. Thomas to San Juan, where Gustavia's boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces invite an unhurried exploration that a single evening rarely allows. Two days in Virgin Gorda follow, from Spanish Town to North Sound, where the island's sheltered bays and striking landscapes reveal themselves at a slower pace. Norman Island arrives next with calm, hidden coves and protected anchorage that invite time to swim and explore before our signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® unfolds along the soft sands of White Bay in Jost van Dyke, where chilled champagne and caviar are served on the sand, followed by an elegant beachside barbecue and long, unhurried hours in the water. The journey concludes in San Juan, where the color and energy of Puerto Rico's capital provide a vibrant and fitting close.

The island has tons of history, beautiful beaches, a fantastic golf course and incredible shopping options.

Nearly every publication written about Virgin Gorda will emphasize the need to visit “The Baths” – don’t miss it! SeaDream generally arrives early and anchors off Spanish Town to give guests an early start to view The Baths before all of the tourists arrive from the neighboring Islands. You may also consider excellent scuba diving options or an opportunity to swim with the dolphins. SeaDream navigates scenically up the coast and arrives in North Sound to anchor just off the Bitter End Yacht Club. Here we offer watersports, land adventures, hiking options with the crew and tenders to the Bitter End! Depending on the voyage, you may also visit Prickly Pear Island for another signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® option with an incredible setting.

Norman Island is located at the southern tip of the British Virgin Islands. It could very well be the very same island reputed to be the inspiration for Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel Treasure Island. It is said that the island was named after a pirate who purchased it at some point during the early 18th century. The island is uninhabited and privately owned by Dr Henry Jarecki. Its area is about 600 acres (2.4 km²), and it is about 2.5 miles (4 km) long. A large harbor is known as "The Bight" offers one of the most protected anchorages in the area. Guests will enjoy some great hiking opportunities as well as snorkeling and scuba diving. Another attractive option may be to check out the Willie T that is generally anchored in the harbor or simply have a beverage at the Pirates Bight Bar.

The BVI’s barefoot island and home of the "Painkiller" drink. Population depends on the month – typically 250-300. This is another SeaDream destination where you may be served Champagne & Caviar Splash® followed by a beach barbecue lunch. A hike is always offered to guests to visit the famous Foxy’s Bar at Great Harbour (hopefully, the boutique is open) or you can stroll a few meters down the beach to the Soggy Dollar Bar. Snorkeling equipment is provided as well as some of our water toys!

voyages.title: Yachting the Bahamas
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Remote anchorages, flamingo-dotted shores, and the unhurried pace of the out islands unfold on this journey from San Juan to Palm Beach, tracing a path through the Dominican Republic and across the Bahamas. Samana offers an early highlight, a deeply scenic bay on the Dominican Republic's northeastern coast where lush hills tumble toward the water and humpback whales gather in the surrounding seas. A day at sea offers a natural pause to unwind on deck before arriving at San Salvador, one of the Bahamas' most remote and rarely visited islands, where pristine reefs, crystalline waters, and an untouched interior create a landscape few travelers ever encounter. Gordon's Beach follows, a secluded Bahamian shore where SeaDream drops anchor for our Champagne & Caviar Splash®, a signature celebration of Champagne, iced caviar, and a leisurely beach barbecue under open skies. Staniel Cay in the Exumas reveals the Bahamas at their most cinematic, where swimming pigs, crystal-clear tidal pools, and a colorful waterfront yacht club have made it one of the archipelago's most celebrated stops. Taino Beach on Grand Bahama offers a final Caribbean interlude before the journey concludes in Palm Beach.

Lying on the northern coast of Samana Bay, Samana is one of the Dominican Republic’s lesser traveled exotic gems. Its natural wonders take the shape of coconut palms contouring the sea, tropical rainforests, brilliant, white-sand beaches hugging the coastline, and charming villages. Discover local markets, dine in seaview restaurants, and perhaps spot some humpback whales. Adventurers can explore the island via ATV tour or by ziplining in Samana Bay.

One of the smallest inhabited islands in the Bahamas, San Salvador boasts sparkling inland lakes, reef-filled sea waters, miles of secluded white-sand beaches, and dive sites teeming with sea life. A stone cross on the shores of Long Bay mark Columbus’s landfall on the island; offshore, an underwater monument designates where La Pinta dropped anchor. Pace yourself to the rhythm of the island with a leisurely swim or bike ride around the bay.

Colorful coral reefs and serene beaches make Long Island a haven for snorkeling, diving, and bone fishing. Relax under the shade of pine trees at Gordon’s Beach, the southernmost white-sand beach on the island. Explore Long Island from the perspective two of its most impressive natural wonders, the Hamilton Caves, dripping with stalactites, and Dean’s Blue Hole, the world’s second-deepest saltwater blue hole, surrounded by limestone bluffs. The island is also home to St. Mary the Virgin Anglican Church, a now-abandoned stone church constructed by the Spanish in the 1600s and reputed to be the oldest in the Bahamas.

As part of the Exuma Cays, Staniel Cay is a magical corner of the Bahamas. Located south of Nassau, this island is an unsung paradise. Visit the infamous swimming pigs at Pig Beach, where numerous pigs race over to get your attention right above crystal-clear waters. Dive or snorkel in the sun-kissed beaches of Exumas and enjoy local dining options for an exclusive look at the Bahamas’ culture and cuisine.

The combination of urban centers and cultural treasures make Palm Beach the perfect getaway. Enter the heart of Africa by visiting the Panther Ridge Conservation Center or get up close and personal with manatees at the Manatee Lagoon. If you’re more into urban sightseeing, visit CityPlace for the top-rated dining, entertainment, and shopping experiences.

voyages.title: Spanish & French Caribbean Discovery
voyages.overview: Overview Ports Staterooms Land Adventures Testimonials Puerto Rico's outer islands set the tone for this roundtrip journey from San Juan, beginning in Culebra, where crystalline waters and an unhurried pace reveal a quieter side of the Caribbean, before continuing to Esperanza, a sun-bleached waterfront village on Vieques' southern coast where the malecón comes alive in the evening, just a short ride from Mosquito Bay, home to one of the world's brightest bioluminescent bays. In St. John, Cruz Bay opens to the protected forests and reef-lined shores of Virgin Islands National Park, where the land meets the sea in near-pristine condition. Marigot follows with the relaxed sophistication of the French side of St. Martin, where open-air markets, waterfront bistros, and a laid-back harbor invite an afternoon of wandering. Continue to St. Barths for an overnight stay in Gustavia, where boutique-lined streets and softly lit terraces take on a more intimate character once the harbor settles into evening. The final stop in Jost van Dyke delivers one of the Caribbean's most memorable afternoons, with our signature Champagne & Caviar Splash® on the soft sands of White Bay, where chilled champagne, caviar, and an elegant beachside barbecue give way to an unhurried afternoon in the water before returning to San Juan.
